Date of Notice: 2026-08-24
Requested Service/CPT: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030

Dear Appeal and Grievance Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (laminotomy/discectomy with decompression of nerve root) dated 2026-08-24. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." This letter, together with the enclosed records, supplies the complete clinical documentation necessary to support medical necessity, and I ask that the denial be reversed.

Governing Policy

I understand that PacificSource applies the following standard to this request. From PacificSource's "Spinal Surgery" clinical guideline: "Prior authorization is required. PacificSource considers spine surgery to be medically necessary when the criteria outlined in Carelon Musculoskeletal Spine Surgery Guideline is met."

Under the referenced Carelon Musculoskeletal Spine Surgery Clinical Appropriateness Guideline, the section titled "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy" identifies, among the qualifying findings, the following: "Radicular pain (with or without demonstrable neurologic deficits) which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of conservative management."

I have not been able to independently confirm the complete remaining text of that section (for example, any separately worded imaging-correlation requirement), and I am not quoting or attributing any language to the plan beyond the two passages quoted above. To the extent additional criteria exist in that section, I ask that PacificSource identify them specifically and confirm whether the enclosed record satisfies each one, or, if any element remains unaddressed, allow the treating surgeon an opportunity for a peer-to-peer discussion before a final decision is issued.

How the Clinical Record Addresses the Denial Reason and the Known Criterion

The original submission apparently did not fully convey the extent of the workup and conservative treatment already completed. The following documentation, which we ask be made part of the appeal file, addresses this gap:

1. Duration and nature of symptoms: The member has experienced 12 months of progressive lower back pain, unrelieved by rest, consistent with a chronic, non-emergent condition rather than an acute event.

2. Conservative management (directly responsive to the "at least 6 weeks of conservative management" criterion quoted above): The member completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 visits, 2026-04-24 through 2026-07-03), including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility training, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the 6-week threshold referenced in the guideline language quoted above.

3. Medication trial: NSAIDs were used for 8 months with inadequate relief.

4. Interventional treatment: A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-30 produced only 3 weeks of partial relief, indicating that non-surgical options have been reasonably exhausted.

5. Imaging findings: MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-07-28 demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root — an anatomic finding at the level and side corresponding to the patient's symptoms.

6. Functional limitation: The member is unable to stand for more than 10 minutes and has radicular pain radiating into the right calf.

7. Physical examination: Positive provocative testing on the affected (right) side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level (L4-L5/L5 nerve root), correlating the imaging findings with objective exam findings.

8. Absence of contraindications: No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

9. Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery, who can be reached for a peer-to-peer review at [Surgeon's Office Phone Number] and whose office NPI/fax is [NPI/Fax Number].

Taken together, this record documents unremitting radicular pain that has not responded to at least 6 weeks of conservative management (in fact, 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy plus 8 months of NSAID therapy and a corticosteroid injection), correlating imaging, and a corresponding neurologic deficit on examination. We respectfully submit that this satisfies the criterion quoted above from the Carelon Musculoskeletal Spine Surgery Guideline as applied by PacificSource, and we ask that PacificSource identify in writing any additional, specific criterion from that guideline that it believes remains unmet, along with the exact guideline language and version relied upon, so that the record can be supplemented if necessary.

Requested Action

1. Reverse the denial and approve CPT 63030 for Skyler Ellison based on the enclosed documentation.
2. If any specific documentation gap remains, please identify it explicitly, in writing, with reference to the exact criterion and guideline version applied, so it can be promptly addressed.
3. If a peer-to-peer conversation would assist in resolving this appeal, please contact Dr. Lindqvist's office at [Surgeon's Office Phone Number] to schedule one.
4. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the applicable internal appeal timeframe, and, if the internal appeal is denied, please provide instructions for requesting an external independent review.

Enclosed Records

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits)
- Medication history (NSAID use, 8 months)
- Corticosteroid injection record (2026-05-30)
- Lumbar spine MRI report (2026-07-28)
- Clinic notes documenting functional limitations and physical examination findings
- Surgeon's operative plan/letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist

I appreciate your prompt attention to this appeal, which I understand must be received by 2027-02-20. Please direct any questions to me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address], or to Dr. Lindqvist's office at [Surgeon's Office Phone Number].

Sincerely,

Skyler Ellison
Member ID: W240749705

Enclosures: as listed above
